title: Parade days, Joe Watson and Al Landry's E-flat clarinet
summary: He describes all-day May parades, fairground bands, and how Al Landry of the Eureka band brought him an E-flat clarinet.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: I mean, you were just talking about the... We played a parade there. Our fellas used to parade from eight in the morning till six in the evening. Uh-huh. All day parade there. Amazons come from, uh... Out the country and everywhere. It was big, big to do over the 30th of May. Me. Uh... They'd have pigments at the fairground. All the day for the cheering. And at night it would be for grown people. They would use brass bands. And, uh... Grandstand. And what they call the tongue. Would be out in the ring. You know what? The tongue.
Oh, yeah. Would be out on the platform. They would build that, uh... Dancy Wire or Ragtime band.

But, uh... You know, I said, Joe Watson. It was the first time he was using the E-flat. You see. Oh, I see. Well, he borrowed the E-flat. Al Landry was the leader of the Eureka band. The original Eureka band. He was working for Warline as an agent selling instruments. And he brought me the E-flat. But I had my E-flat along with me. And, uh... I played the E-flat. And then I couldn't take it on. But before that I played all the E-flat. Oh, I see.
